Assessment.content: Watery diarrhea, intermittent left lower quadrant cramps, early vomiting and subjective fever, tolerating fluids, no blood per rectum or hematemesis support diagnosis of acute gastroenteritis
Assessment.source_text: Suspected acute gastroenteritis—watery diarrhea, intermittent LLQ cramps, early vomiting and subjective fever; tolerating fluids; no blood PR/hematemesis.

Plan_of_Care.content: Conservative management with maintenance of oral hydration
Use oral rehydration salts such as Dioralyte from pharmacy
Paracetamol 2 tablets up to 4 times per day for first few days if feverish or weak
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Paracetamol 2 tabs up to 4x/day for first few days if feverish/weak

Plan_of_Care.content: If not improved in 3–4 days, follow up and if symptoms persist, send stool sample for testing
